title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Residential PM<sub>1</sub> Prediction in Zagreb (Croatia): Identifying Key Predictors and Indoor/Outdoor Dynamics
summary: A Zagreb residential pilot measured paired indoor and outdoor PM1 in 103 samples. Gradient-boosted regression explained about 65% of test-set variation in indoor PM1; outdoor PM1, infiltration and resuspension ranked among leading predictors. Winter outdoor peaks did not coincide with higher indoor medians. This local observational result is not a causal estimate or broadly validated exposure rule.
ai_technology: Gradient-boosted regression predicted indoor PM1 from paired environmental and dwelling variables; SHAP attributed model influence.
organization: Institute for Medical Research and Occupational Health,; Faculty of Chemical Engineering, University of Zagreb,; Srebrnjak Children's Hospital,; The School of Medicine, Catholic University of Croatia

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: The study evaluated predictions on a held-out portion of 103 paired residential samples and used SHAP to rank predictors.
evidence.unknown: Small local pilot; model associations do not establish causal effects and may not generalize beyond sampled residences.
